Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Adesto, Domine, populo` where 1862 reads `AD6sto, D6mine, p6nulo`; 1962 reads `Nicomedis` where 1862 reads `Nicom6ais`; 1962 reads `suscipiens,` where 1862 reads `suscfpiens,`; 1962 reads `misericordiam` where 1862 reads `misenc6rdiam`; 1962 reads `patrociniis adiuvetur. Per Dominum` where 1862 reads `Batrociniis adjuv6tur. rer >6minum`; 1962 has `Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets no comma after the `ut`; the 1962 does; 1862 and Mame print the j-orthography where the 1962 prints i; 1862 conclusion is the short cue; the 1962 at no. 3632 writes it out in full (and at no. 3617 prints the short cue); 1862 text-layer letterforms are damaged throughout (accents recognised as digits, drop capital mangled, one p read as B and one P as r); every damaged word is clean in the 1922 Mame at the same place. Corroboration: 1922 Mame, printed p. 715, artifact PDF p. 829, read on the text layer; alignment ratio 0.702, differences: 1962 reads `Adesto,` where 1922 Mame reads `pEsTo,`; 1962 has nothing there; 1922 Mame has `:`; 1962 reads `praeclara` where 1922 Mame reads `preclara`; 1962 has `nostrum Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.`; 1922 Mame has nothing there. Second 1962 printing at no. 3617 confirms the body..

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Adesto, Domine, populo tuo: ut, beati Nicomedis Martyris tui merita
praeclara suscipiens, ad impetrandam misericordiam tuam semper ejus
patrociniis adjuvetur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
